product.name: Street Food Explorer Community
product.tagline: Foodies review street food stalls by locality; hidden gems surface via community upvotes

sections.problem_statement: Street food enthusiasts struggle to find hygienic, authentic, and high-quality stalls in urban Indian neighborhoods due to fragmented, unreliable reviews on mainstream platforms. Existing platforms prioritize high-budget restaurants and paid ads, effectively burying the authentic, hyper-local vendors that define the street food experience. This product solves the discovery gap by gamifying community-led verification of stalls based on taste, hygiene, and value, ensuring hidden gems surface organically.
target_users: Arjun, a 24-year-old Corporate Analyst who finds mainstream delivery apps too expensive and lacks authentic, affordable local food recommendations.
Priya, a 30-year-old Content Creator who struggles to find visually appealing and 'viral-worthy' street food spots to feature in her hyperlocal food vlogs.
Rahul, a 45-year-old Local Resident who is deeply skeptical of street food hygiene and needs community-verified social proof before trying a new stall.
user_stories: As a food explorer, I want to filter stalls by 'Hygiene Rating' provided by community members so that I can eat safely without compromising on taste.
As a local food blogger, I want to upload geotagged photos and short-form video reviews so that I can establish my authority as a local food expert.
As a street food vendor, I want to claim my stall profile so that I can showcase my menu and respond to customer feedback directly.
As a community member, I want to 'Upvote' a hidden gem so that it gains visibility in the 'Top Rated in Locality' feed.
As a user, I want to save a list of 'Must-Try' stalls to my profile so that I can easily plan my weekend food trails.
mvp_features: Geotagged Stall Discovery: A map-based interface showing stalls within a 3km radius to drive immediate footfall.
Community Verification Score: A proprietary scoring algorithm based on user-submitted hygiene, taste, and price tags to build trust.
Stall Claiming Portal: A simple mobile-first flow for vendors to verify their location and update their operating hours.
Gamified Leaderboards: A 'Street Food Local Hero' badge system to incentivize users to contribute high-quality, authentic reviews.
Hygiene Check-in: A mandatory checkbox survey during review submission focusing on FSSAI compliance awareness (cleanliness, gloves, water source).
Short-form Video Integration: Support for 15-second video uploads to showcase stall ambiance and food preparation.
future_features: AI-powered Menu Translator: Translates regional street food names into multiple languages for better accessibility.
Digital Loyalty Program: A unified stamp-card system for street food vendors to encourage repeat visits.
Hyperlocal Group Orders: A feature allowing users in the same office park to pool orders from a popular stall.
FSSAI Compliance Verification: Direct API integration with FSSAI databases to display official vendor licenses.
success_metrics: DAU/MAU Ratio: Target 30% by Month 6 — indicates strong habit formation and community engagement.
Stall Coverage: 500 verified stalls in 3 target PIN codes by Month 3 — ensures sufficient density for user utility.
Review Contribution Rate: 15% of active users posting at least one review monthly — measures the health of the community engine.
Average Session Duration: 4 minutes by Month 4 — indicates users are actively exploring and reading community insights.
assumptions: Users are willing to contribute high-quality content without monetary incentives beyond social recognition.
Street food vendors are increasingly smartphone-literate and interested in digital visibility.
The target urban demographic values authentic, affordable experiences over premium dining during economic downturns.
risks: Content spam/fake reviews → Implement a robust moderation queue and 'Trust Score' for users based on review history.
Safety/Hygiene incidents → Include a clear legal disclaimer regarding FSSAI standards and a reporting mechanism for unsafe stalls.
Low vendor adoption → Launch with a 'Street Food Ambassador' program that physically visits and onboards vendors for free.
sections.go_to_market: Launch with a 'Neighborhood Takeover' strategy in three high-density food hubs in Bangalore to create immediate buzz. Use a referral loop where influencers get 'Local Legend' status for bringing the first 100 stalls onto the platform. Acquire the first 1,000 power users via Reddit community partnerships and hyperlocal WhatsApp groups.
sections.tech_stack_suggestion: Use a no-code stack like Bubble.io for rapid iteration and frontend management. Integrate Google Maps Platform API for location services and Firebase for real-time community engagement features. Architecture will be a serverless, event-driven model to keep operational costs low while scaling for peak evening hours.
sections.monetisation: Implement a 'Featured Stall' advertising model where vendors pay ₹499/month for top-of-feed placement. Introduce a 'Premium Explorer' subscription at ₹99/year for exclusive access to curated food trails and early-bird event invites. Future revenue will come from commission-based lead generation for food festivals and corporate catering partnerships.
